la:noun:OB.html:
ŏb (old form obs, v. III.), prep. with acc. (in late Lat. also with the abl.:
OB PERPETVO EIVS ERGA SE AMORE,) [Osc. op; kindr. with Sanscr. api; Gr. ἐπί].
Lit.
With verbs of motion, towards, to (only ante-class.): IS TERTHS DIEBVS OB PORTVM OBVAGVLATVM ITO, let him go before his house to summon him, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. portum, p. 233 Müll.: ob Romam legiones ducere, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Müll. (Ann. v. 295 Vahl.); cf.: ob Troiam duxit, (Incert. libr. v. 5 Vahl.): cujus ob os Grai ora obvertebant sua, Poët. ap. ; and ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 211 Rib.).—
With verbs of rest, about, before, in front of, over (in Cic.): follem sibi obstringit ob gulam,: lanam ob oculum habere,: ob oculos mihi caliginem obstitisse,before my eyes,: mors ob oculos saepe versata est,; : ignis qui est ob os offusus,.—
Transf., to indicate the object or cause, on account of, for, because of, by reason of, etc.
In gen. (freq. and class.): etiam ob stultitiam tuam te tueris?do you still defend yourself with regard to your folly?: pretium ob stultitiam fero,; : ob eam rem iratus,on that account,: neu quid ob eam rem succenseat,; : Mi. Ob eam rem? De. Ob eam, . 9, 20: ob rem nullam,: hanc Epicurus rationem induxit ob eam rem, quod veritus est, ne, etc.,: ob eam causam, quod, etc.,: quam ob causam venerant, : non solum ob eam causam fieri volui, quod, etc.,: ob hanc causam, quod,: nec ob aliam causam ullam, etc.,: ob meas injurias,; cf.: quodnam ob facinus?: ob peccatum hoc. v. 37: ob malefacta haec,: ob illam injuriam,: ob aliquod emolumentum suum,: (eum) ac Troiam misi ob defendendam Graeciam, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 362 Vahl.): ob rem judicandam pecuniam adcipere,; ; ; ; ; : nec meliores ob eam scientiam nec beatiores esse possumus,on account of, for that knowledge,: ob eam (amicitiam) summā fide servatam,: is igitur dicitur ab Amulio ob labefactandi regni timorem, ad Tiberim exponi jussus esse,: unius ob iram Prodimur,; cf.: saevae memorem Junonis ob iram,; cf. also: aut ob avaritiam aut miserā ambitione laborat,: barbarus eum quidam palam ob iram interfecti ab eo domini obtruncat,: non noxā neque ob metum,: Germanicum mortem ob rem publicam obiisse,for the republic,: cum quibus ob rem pecuniariam disceptabat,.—
In partic.
In consideration of, in return for, instead of (mostly ante-class.): ob asinos ferre argentum,; : quin arrhabonem a me accepisti ob mulierem?: ager oppositus est pignori Ob decem minas,: talentum magnum ob unam fabulam datum esse, C. Gracch. ap. : pecuniam ob absolvendum accipere,: pecuniam ob delicta dare,.—
Ob rem, like ex re (opp. frustra), to the purpose, with advantage, profitably, usefully (very rare): An. Non pudet Vanitatis? Do. Minime, dum ob rem, Ter Phorm. 3, 2, 41: verum id frustra an ob rem faciam, in vostrā manu situm est,.—
Ob industriam, on purpose, intentionally, ; (, de industriā); cf. .—
Quam ob rem, also written in one word, quamobrem, on which account, wherefore, therefore, hence, accordingly; a very freq. particle of transition, esp. in Cic.: quam ob rem id primum videamus, quatenus, etc.,: quam ob rem utrique nostrūm gratum admodum feceris,; 2, 10; 3, 12; 4, 15; ; et saep.—
Ob id, ob hoc, ob haec, ob ea, ob quae, on that account, therefore (not ante-Aug.).
Ob id: ignaris hostibus et ob id quietis,; ; ; ; : ob id ipsum,.—
Ob hoc: ob hoc cum omnia neglecta apud hostes essent,; ; ; cf.: ob hoc miserior,. —
Ob haec: ob haec cum legatos mitti placuisset,; ; ; —
Ob ea: ob ea consul Albinus senatum de foedere consulebat,.—
Ob quae: ob quae posterum diem reus petivit,; .—
In composition, the b of ob remains unchanged before vowels and most consonants; only before p, f, c, g, is assimilation more common: oppeto, offero, occido, ogganio, etc.—An ancient form obs, analogous to abs, is implied in obs-olesco and os-tendo.—In signification, that of direction towards, or of existence at or before a thing is predominant, although it likewise gives to the simple verb the accessory notion of against: obicere, opponere, obrogare.

la:prep:ob.gloss: in the direction of, to, towards
senses: in the direction of, to, towards
on account of, according to, because of, due to, for (the purpose of)
